skill.name: biorxiv-database

content.value_statement: Researchers need current preprint metadata without manual browsing. This skill searches bioRxiv, filters results, exports metadata, and downloads PDFs when requested.
actual_capabilities: Search bioRxiv records by keywords across titles, abstracts, or author fields.
Filter preprints by date range and supported bioRxiv subject category.
Find papers by author name within a selected date window.
Retrieve detailed metadata for a specific bioRxiv DOI.
Export formatted search results to a local JSON file.
Download a bioRxiv PDF for a provided DOI and output path.
limitations: It only searches bioRxiv and does not include medRxiv or journal databases.
Keyword matching is simple substring filtering, not semantic search.
Large date ranges may be slow because results are fetched before filtering.
PDF downloads assume version 1 unless metadata provides another version.

use_cases.title: Track New Papers in a Research Area
use_cases.description: Search recent bioRxiv records for selected terms and categories, then review titles, authors, abstracts, and links.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Systematic Review Seed Set
use_cases.description: Collect preprint metadata across a controlled date range and export results for screening or citation workflows.

use_cases.title: Monitor Author or Lab Output
use_cases.description: Find recent bioRxiv preprints matching an author name and save the results for periodic tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Keyword Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search bioRxiv for recent preprints about CRISPR gene editing from the last 90 days and summarize the top matches.

prompt_templates.title: Category Filtered Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Narrow a topic to one bioRxiv subject area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find bioRxiv preprints about single cell sequencing in the genomics category from January 2025 through June 2025.

prompt_templates.title: Author Monitoring
prompt_templates.scenario: Track publications from a named researcher.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search bioRxiv for papers by author Smith during the past year and list titles, dates, DOIs, and categories.

prompt_templates.title: Review Dataset Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a bioRxiv literature review dataset for organoids and tissue engineering from 2024, limited to bioengineering, and save the results.

output_examples.input: Search for CRISPR papers in genomics from 2024.
output_examples.output: A result summary with paper titles, authors, publication dates, DOIs, abstracts when included, and bioRxiv links.
A single paper record with title, author list, date, category, version, abstract, and available full-text links.

output_examples.input: Download the PDF for a selected DOI.
output_examples.output: A saved PDF file at the requested path, with a success or failure message.

best_practices: Use specific date ranges and categories to reduce result volume and API traffic.
Save results to a project folder so searches are reproducible and easy to review.
Review returned metadata before using downloaded PDFs in analysis workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad multi-year keyword searches when a focused range will work.
Do not treat bioRxiv preprints as peer-reviewed journal publications.
Do not overwrite important local files when selecting output paths.

faq.question: Does this skill search all biomedical literature?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on bioRxiv preprints and does not query PubMed, medRxiv, Scopus, or Web of Science.

faq.question: Can it download full papers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can download a bioRxiv PDF when you provide a DOI and output file path.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. It calls the public bioRxiv API and bioRxiv content URLs.

faq.question: Can it search abstracts?
faq.answer: Yes. Keyword searches can check titles, abstracts, and author fields.

faq.question: Does it perform semantic ranking?
faq.answer: No. It filters returned records by exact keyword matching and optional category or date constraints.

faq.question: What format are results saved in?
faq.answer: Search results are saved as structured JSON when an output file is provided.
